items.detail: Safe only if the weather API deduplicates on the X-Request-Id header, which the change does not show.

items.title: Timeout is applied per attempt, not per forecast
items.detail: Worst-case time per forecast grows with WEATHER_MAX_RETRIES and the backoff cap of four seconds.

items.title: WeatherError constructor changed
items.detail: It takes an optional retryAfterMs argument; other callers that build the error should still compile.

items.title: Backoff values are hard coded
items.detail: 3 retries, 250 ms base and a 4,000 ms cap. Confirm they fit the rate limits of the provider.

items.title: Tests cover the happy path only
items.detail: There is no test for a response with a Retry-After header that is larger than the cap.

visual.heading: What changes for callers of the weather client

items.text: Temporary failures (HTTP 429 and every 5xx) are retried automatically with exponential backoff and full jitter.
The Retry-After header wins over the computed delay when the provider sends one.
One request id key per forecast is sent on every attempt, so a retried forecast cannot be applied twice.
WEATHER_MAX_RETRIES controls how many retries happen; the default is three.
Everything else, such as a 400 or a 404, still fails at once and reaches the caller unchanged.

visual.problem: Forecast requests sometimes fail with a 429 or a 503 during traffic spikes, and callers have to retry by hand, which is slow, error prone and sometimes asks the same question twice.
visual.goal: Retry temporary failures automatically with exponential backoff and jitter, and make sure that a retried forecast can never be applied twice by the weather provider.

points.text: Exponential backoff with full jitter between attempts
Retry-After is respected when the provider sends it
One request id key per forecast, shared by every attempt
New unit tests cover the retry rules and the limits

points.text: 429 and 5xx responses are retried with full-jitter backoff, up to three times by default.
The Retry-After header is respected, capped at four seconds.
One request id key per forecast keeps retried forecasts from being applied twice.
WeatherError carries the retry-after value; check callers that build it.
New unit tests cover the policy; the author reports that they pass.

visual.closing: Review the request id handling and the timeout behaviour first, then the new tests.
